items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 67:1
items.html: The vessels are called letters, and 'the vowel points, like the movement of the letters,' means that the aspect of the light that moves the vessels is only the illumination of the vessels themselves — that is, there is no illumination of Hochma in them, but only from the aspect of Bina and below, called the illumination of the vessels, as is known. And they are the vowel points of the HaVaYaH in Holam, Tzere, Kamatz, Tzere: the Holam indicates the lights of Yechida and Chaya in the name, which are not clothed in the vessels but above them, like the Holam, which stands above the letters. And the Tzere indicates concealed Hassadim, for the two points of the Tzere indicate Hochma and Bina, at the time when Bina is at the back of Hochma; hence there is no third point beneath them, which is the Daat that couples these Hochma and Bina. Thus the Hei of the HaVaYaH, punctuated with a Tzere, indicates the aspect of Hassadim concealed and hidden from the aspect of the illumination of Hochma. And the Kamatz beneath the Vav of the HaVaYaH indicates ZA, which is compressed from the illumination of Hochma. And the Hei with the Tzere indicates also concealed Hassadim, like the first Hei. (Page 313, Item 42; and in Or Pnimi, s.v. 'punctuated').
